title: Inlining: caller absorbs accumulate (running example §4)
summary_caption: Inlining: legality, then InlineCost against a threshold, then clone with argument remap — bottom-up, so callees are simplified before their callers.

nodes.label:
accumulate(a, n, k)
loop: sum += a[i] * k
ret sum

caller(a, n)
call accumulate(a, n, 4)
ret

frames.caption: Running example, stage 4: caller passes the constant 4 as k. The Inliner must decide this call site.
The Inliner is a CGSCC pass over the call graph, bottom-up: the callee accumulate is visited and simplified first.
Then caller. Its one call site is examined: should accumulate(a, n, 4) be inlined here?
Step 1, legality and mandatory checks: no varargs mismatch, no noinline, no alwaysinline forcing it. Legal, so the cost model decides.
Step 2, profitability: InlineCost tallies the body, minus a bonus because argument k = 4 is a constant that will fold code away. Under threshold: inline.
The call is replaced by a clone of the callee: blocks keep their names plus an .i suffix, and the ret turns into a branch to accumulate.exit.
During cloning the value map rewired formal %k to the actual 4: compare the callee's mul by k with the clone's mul %0, 4.
The payoff of context: with 4 visible, InstCombine folds mul %0, 4 into shl %0, 2. No call boundary blocks the optimization.
Inlining added no new call sites to the worklist, so caller is done. accumulate itself survives: it is still externally visible.
